possible_mappings.confidence: UNVERIFIED (disfavored; two separate SetKey calls suggest different pointers)

rust_comparison.binary_behavior: Two separate pointers passed to SetKeyPair; content-to-pointer mapping UNKNOWN
rust_comparison.notes: Rust uses same 32 bytes for both directions. Binary takes two separate pointers. Whether the two pointers point to different halves is unconfirmed, but the existence of SetKeyPair as a two-argument function suggests different keys.

aes_key_mapping.required_experiment: Dynamic execution: breakpoint on SetKeyPair (0x1006a630), inspect pointer args relative to GetKey buffer

identity_encoding_in_hash.evidence: Wire byte-swap at 0x100667b0; binary reads raw bytes from obj+0x8

password_encoding_in_hash.evidence: Password passed as caller (ptr, len) at 0x10060340/0x10060c80; no transformation inside shelper.dll; caller not traced

rust_comparison.rust_identity: encode_identity() produces UTF-16BE (wire format); if hash input is internal UTF-16LE, this differs
rust_comparison.classification: INFERRED_MISMATCH (password); PARTIAL (identity — needs wire vs hash disambiguation)
rust_comparison.notes: Phase 10.5 corrected identity to UTF-16LE for hash; but encode_identity() actually produces UTF-16BE. If binary hashes internal UTF-16LE buffer, there is a mismatch. If binary hashes wire-format UTF-16BE, there is no mismatch. This needs direct verification.

password_encoding.required_experiment: Dynamic: breakpoint on 0x10060340, inspect identity buffer bytes for known test string (e.g., 'A' → UTF-16LE=41 00, UTF-16BE=00 41)

assumptions.description: context+0x20 = A on client / B on server
assumptions.basis: FUN_10060410/FUN_10060d80 disassembly: both write context+0x20 after mod_exp call
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: u computation differs → S differs → handshake failure

assumptions.description: Password is UTF-16LE (same source as identity)
assumptions.basis: Identity is UTF-16LE; RvROLClient.dll has MultiByteToWideChar imports

assumptions.description: Two halves of 64-byte secret are used for enc and dec respectively
assumptions.basis: SetKeyPair takes two separate pointers; unlikely to pass same pointer twice
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: If same key used for both directions, one direction will fail decryption

assumptions.description: k = SHA-1(N||PAD192(g)) is the active multiplier
assumptions.basis: FUN_10060810/FUN_10060ec0 referenced from SRP-6a descriptors; FUN_100607d0 (k=3) is dead code
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Different k → different S → handshake failure

assumptions.description: Identity hash input is UTF-16LE (internal form, not UTF-16BE wire form)
assumptions.basis: Wire byte-swap analysis: stored as UTF-16LE, swapped to UTF-16BE for wire
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: If hash input is actually UTF-16BE, Rust encode_identity() matches and no mismatch exists
